lesson.text: Quick memory: where is the air clearer in a smoky room? (Low down.) Today: escaping a fire, and stop, drop and roll.
Every home needs a fire plan: two ways out of every room, and a meeting point outside, like a tree or a lamp post.
When the alarm beeps, get low under the smoke. Before you open a door, touch it with the back of your hand. Warm? Use the other way.
Close doors behind you: a closed door slows down fire and smoke. Get out, stay out, and call {number} from outside.
If your clothes catch fire: stop, drop to the ground, cover your face with your hands, and roll over and over until the flames are out.
Try it in the world: open the practice house and do the fire drill. Next: the fire extinguisher, on the Big track.

exercises.prompt: The smoke alarm beeps. What do you do first?
exercises.explain: Get low under the smoke and get out.

exercises.prompt: Close doors behind you as you get out.
exercises.hint: What does a closed door slow down?
exercises.explain: True: a closed door slows down fire and smoke.

exercises.prompt: Where do you go when you are out?
exercises.explain: Go to your meeting point, so the grown-ups know you are safe.

exercises.prompt: How do you check a door before you open it?
choices: touch it with the back of your hand
exercises.explain: Touch it with the back of your hand. Warm means fire may be behind it.

exercises.prompt: A warm door is safe to open.
exercises.hint: What could be behind a warm door?
exercises.explain: False: a warm door can mean fire behind it. Use the other way out.

exercises.prompt: Clothes on fire: put it in order.
exercises.hint: Its name tells you most of it.
exercises.explain: Stop, drop to the ground, cover your face, and roll.

exercises.prompt: Why close the door behind you?
choices: it slows the fire and smoke
exercises.explain: A closed door slows down the fire and the smoke.

exercises.prompt: Your bedroom door is warm. What now?
exercises.hint: Every room has two ways out in the plan.
exercises.explain: Leave a warm door shut and use the other way out.

exercises.prompt: How many ways out should every room have in your fire plan?
exercises.hint: One, and one more if the first is blocked.
exercises.explain: Two: if one is blocked, you use the other.

exercises.prompt: Do it, or never do it?
items: go back in for a toy
exercises.explain: Get low and call from outside. Never go back in, never hide.

exercises.prompt: Running when your clothes are on fire helps.
exercises.hint: What does running bring to a fire?
exercises.explain: False: running fans the flames. Stop, drop and roll.
